solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Lose sight of minute special supply

indicators.note: read as the adverb of supple, the letters of special are bent into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone misses a tiny but particular delivery of goods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supply' looks like a noun, but it is the adverb from supple ('in a supple way'), which is why it signals an anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: To mislay something is to lose track of it, to lose sight of where it went.

clue.text: Nightmare scenarios because of copper having picked up bribe

parts.note: in can mean because of, as in 'in that'
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

indicators.note: picking something up by ear points to a word heard rather than read

parts.note: to bribe is to buy someone

explanation.surface: A tale of a corrupt police officer caught taking a backhander.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' suggests a policeman but gives the chemical symbol CU; BI is how BUY is heard.
explanation.definitionFit: Incubi are demons said to visit sleepers, the stuff of bad dreams, so the plural fits nightmare scenarios.

clue.text: East Indian queen cutting sucker on climbing plant

indicators.note: one piece cutting another is placed inside it
in a down entry climbing means reading upwards, so the word is reversed

parts.note: a mug is a gullible person, a sucker
a rani is an Indian queen or a raja's wife

explanation.surface: An Indian queen trims a shoot from a climbing plant in the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sucker' and 'climbing plant' both sound horticultural, but sucker is a dupe, MUG, reversed to GUM by 'climbing', and ERANI goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The geranium is a common flowering garden plant, the cranesbill and its relatives.

clue.text: Clock whopping bill that's picked up

parts.note: whopping means very big

indicators.note: in a down entry picked up means lifted from the bottom, so the word reads upwards

parts.note: neb is an old word for a bird's beak or bill

explanation.surface: A shockingly large bill that someone has to collect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picked up' feels like a homophone signal, but here it lifts NEB so it reads BEN upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Big Ben is the famous clock tower bell at Westminster, used by extension for the clock itself.

clue.text: Leader of dissenting group ousted in lawsuit

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter, here the one to be dropped
ousted means thrown out, so the opening letter is removed

parts.note: a faction is a breakaway or dissenting group within a party

explanation.surface: A rebel group's chief is deposed in a court case.
explanation.definitionFit: A legal action is a case brought in court, the same thing as a suit at law.

clue.text: Dodgy courier carrying unknown old money overseas

indicators.note: one piece carrying another holds it inside
dodgy means unreliable or out of order, so the letters of courier are jumbled

parts.note: in algebra x, y and z stand for unknowns, here Z

explanation.surface: A shady courier smuggling foreign cash across borders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dodgy' rearranges COURIER into CRUEIRO, and 'carrying' puts Z inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Brazil used this unit of currency until the real replaced it in the 1990s, so it is a former foreign currency.

clue.text: Bendy cable originally installed by local electrician

parts.note: flex is the everyday British word for an insulated electric lead

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letters of the next four words

explanation.surface: A tradesman fitting a pliable cable in someone's home.
explanation.definitionFit: Something pliable that bends easily without breaking is described by this word.

clue.text: Gross present almost pops

parts.note: gross can mean obese, fat

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter is cut

parts.note: to be present is to be here

explanation.surface: A disgusting gift that very nearly explodes.
explanation.definitionFit: Pops is an informal name for one's dad, a male parent.

clue.text: Extended line replacing opening in poem

indicators.note: one piece replacing the opening of a word takes the place of its first letter

parts.note: a song can be a poem or verse

explanation.surface: A lengthened line swapped into the start of some verse.
explanation.definitionFit: Something drawn out or prolonged in time or length is described by this word.

clue.text: Garment's bound to fit

parts.note: to bound is to leap or jump
to suit is to fit or be right for

explanation.surface: Someone's clothing is certain to fit them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bound' reads as 'sure', but here it is a leap.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-piece outfit of trousers and top joined together is an item of clothing.

clue.text: Left bar in outskirts of arty state capital

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another
the outskirts of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: to bar is to ban

explanation.surface: A bar on the edge of a bohemian part of a state's main city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' feels like a pub; here it is a prohibition, BAN.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the seat of government of New York State, a US state capital.

clue.text: Given seating arranged –

indicators.note: arranged means put in a new order, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Seats have been allocated, and the sentence trails off with a dash.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the dash at the end of the clue, which looks like punctuation.
explanation.definitionFit: The printed dash is a minus symbol, the mark showing subtraction or a value below zero.

clue.text: European city to miss out of conversation?

indicators.note: of conversation means as heard in speech, so the words are said aloud

parts.note: to miss out on something is to lose it

explanation.surface: Asking whether a city is one to skip when making small talk.
explanation.definitionFit: Toulouse is a large city in south-west France, so a city in Europe.

clue.text: Buddy's run into addict

indicators.note: one piece run into another is placed inside it

parts.note: a fiend is an addict or devotee, as in a dope fiend
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A pal has bumped into a drug user.
explanation.definitionFit: A buddy is a mate or pal, a close companion.

clue.text: One King James maybe upset a PM

indicators.note: in a down entry upset means turned upside down, so it reads upwards

parts.note: one is I as a Roman numeral
Lear is Shakespeare's king
Sid James was a British comedy actor, star of the Carry On films

explanation.surface: One version of the King James Bible annoys a prime minister.
explanation.walkthrough: 'King James' suggests the Bible; King is LEAR and James is SID JAMES, an English comic actor; 'upset' reverses ILEARSID.
explanation.definitionFit: Benjamin Disraeli was twice Conservative prime minister under Queen Victoria.

clue.text: Guide tense in river — a sign to go back

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another
read here as the opening letter of the sign going to the back of the word; the plain sense, read the word backwards, does not work

parts.note: an omen is a sign or portent
T is the grammar abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: Directions for steering a boat upstream on a river.
explanation.walkthrough: A setter's slip, which Monk owned up to on fifteensquared: reversing OMEN gives NEMO and so NEMTOR. Only sending OMEN's first letter to the back, giving MENO, makes the wordplay work. His original clue was 'Guide followers by hill' (MEN + TOR).
explanation.definitionFit: A trusted adviser who steers a less experienced person is a guide to them.

clue.text: Tune in or out — no charge for this

indicators.note: out means not in order, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Advice to switch a radio on or off, with no fee to listen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charge' suggests a fee, but the definition means electrical charge.
explanation.definitionFit: This subatomic particle has zero electric charge, hence its name meaning little neutral one.

clue.text: Imagine bodily shape

definitions.meaning: to imagine is to picture or suppose, as in 'I reckoned so'
a person's physique or form, the outline of their body

explanation.definitionFit: The word works both as a verb for supposing something and as a noun for one's physique.

clue.text: Short outfit is, sadly, altered meticulously

indicators.note: altered means changed, so the letters are rearranged
short means cut down, so the last letter of outfit is dropped

explanation.surface: A skimpy outfit has unfortunately been tailored with great care.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' docks OUTFIT to OUTFI, and 'altered' rearranges OUTFIISSADLY. 'sadly' looks like the signal but is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something with fussy attention to every detail is doing it with great care.

clue.text: Fox News literally cutting subscription by cents

indicators.note: one piece cutting another goes inside it

parts.note: a subscription is a fee paid
taken literally, news is the plural of new, and new is N, so two Ns

explanation.surface: A TV news network is dropping its subscription price by a few cents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fox News' reads as the TV channel, but Fox is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The fennec is a small desert fox of North Africa with very large ears.

clue.text: Creature found in Blenheim Palace

indicators.note: found in means the letters sit inside the following words

explanation.surface: An animal discovered roaming the grand English stately home.
explanation.walkthrough: Blenheim Palace is a grand stately home in Oxfordshire, birthplace of Churchill.
explanation.definitionFit: The impala is an African antelope, so an animal.

clue.text: Dawn's second service

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a second
RN is the Royal Navy, one of the armed services

explanation.surface: A woman named Dawn's second church service of the day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dawn' looks like a woman's name; it is daybreak.
explanation.definitionFit: Morn is a poetic word for morning, the start of the day.

clue.text: Continue with bodyguard, ultimately a hired thug

parts.note: to go on is to continue

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: Carrying on with a bodyguard who is, in the end, a paid heavy.
explanation.walkthrough: GOONDA is a word from Indian English, borrowed from Hindi.
explanation.definitionFit: In Indian and South Asian English the word means a ruffian or hooligan paid to commit violence.

clue.text: United crept up unexpectedly — that's a blow

parts.note: U is the abbreviation for United, as in football club names

indicators.note: unexpectedly suggests things turned out differently, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A football team sneaked up the table by surprise, a shock to rivals.
explanation.definitionFit: This upward punch to the chin is a kind of strike in boxing.

clue.text: Be subject to foreign articles outside India

indicators.note: the articles go outside, around, the other piece

parts.note: un and le are French articles, der is German
I is India in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone is bound by rules set out in overseas newspaper pieces about India.
explanation.walkthrough: 'articles' suggests newspaper pieces but means grammatical articles.
explanation.definitionFit: Lying beneath something, being its basis, is to be under it, the subject sense of lying below.

clue.text: Bird perhaps thrashing about?

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: a ten-nil scoreline is an example of a thrashing in football

explanation.surface: A bird flapping wildly, possibly caught.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thrashing about' reads as flailing; it is a heavy defeat (TEN-NIL) turned 'about'.
explanation.definitionFit: The linnet is a small brown finch, a songbird.
